_layer: IDENTITY (EXAMPLE). The never-claim list, in machine-checkable form. engine/lib/check_cv.py enforces these on every CV and cover letter.
_how_to_write_your_own: The highest-value question in setup is: what would a JD ask for that you would have to admit you have not done? Every honest answer becomes a guardrail. These are the rules that stop the system lying on your behalf when it is optimizing for a keyword match.

_schema.pattern: regex that, if found, is a violation
_schema.message: what is wrong AND what the truth is - the message is what you will read at 1am, so make it useful
_schema.allow_context: optional regex; if it matches the window around an occurrence, THAT occurrence is exonerated
_schema.requires: optional regex; if it matches anywhere in the document, the rule does not fire at all

_working_rule: A guardrail firing on legitimate text is a bug in the PATTERN, not in the CV. Add the case to guardrail_tests.json, then loosen allow_context here. NEVER reword a CV to slip past a guardrail - that inverts the whole mechanism.

guardrails._demonstrates: TITLE CEILING, with the two exemptions you will actually need: naming the role you are applying FOR, and naming a senior stakeholder you worked WITH.
guardrails.message: VP/SVP self-label: highest real title is Director of Data Platform

guardrails._demonstrates: A FIGURE THAT DRIFTED. Old CVs keep resurrecting a stale number; pin the wrong one and state the right one.
guardrails.message: stale platform cost-savings figure: the defensible number is ~$250K/yr

guardrails._demonstrates: A TOOL NEVER USED HANDS-ON. Keyword-matching will happily add these; you cannot defend them in an interview.
guardrails.message: streaming tooling never used hands-on: batch pipelines and Airflow only

guardrails._demonstrates: A CLAIM SOMEONE ELSE OWNED, with a negation exemption so an honest disclaimer still passes.
guardrails.message: P&L ownership claim: the business unit owned P&L, not the platform team

guardrails._demonstrates: A TERM THAT MUST BE DEFINED at first mention. Uses `requires`: the rule stands down entirely if the definition appears anywhere.
guardrails.message: Nightjar must be defined as the internal data catalog at first mention - it means nothing to an outside reader

guardrails._demonstrates: A TENURE FIGURE that must stay consistent - with the exemption you WILL need. Durations appear all over a CV ('10 years later', 'over 3 years') and only the candidate's own tenure is the claim being guarded.
guardrails.message: experience is always stated as 12 years

guardrails._demonstrates: A BANNED WORD. Delete this rule if your setup allows 'Present' in date ranges.
guardrails.message: 'Present' in a date range: use the configured Mon YYYY - Mon YYYY format
